stories.text: Henry Robert Clifton laid the school's cornerstone on 3 November 1871, and it opened in April 1872 with 48 children; a night school for men began a year later. It closed in 1956, when new schools were built on the estate, and is now the village hall.

stories.text: The red-brick dovecote on the green was built in the early 18th century for the Clifton family's farming estate.[^cvra] It is said to be one of the largest in England, with about 2,300 nesting places; pigeons were kept for winter meat.[^walk] A stone tablet on its side remembers the men of the village who died in the First World War.[^roll] It is listed Grade II.

stories.text: The Clifton family held the manor of Clifton from the late 13th century, and this was their manor house.[^s1] Sir Gervase Clifton largely rebuilt it between 1778 and 1797, partly to designs by John Carr of York.[^s1] In 1958 the family sold it, ending 700 years of ownership; it became a girls' grammar school, and is now two houses.[^s1] The hall itself dates from the late 16th century and is listed Grade I. In its grounds are a brick ice house of the mid-18th century, the vaulted remains of a curved garden stairway, a pair of Coade stone lions of the early 19th century, and the late 18th-century stable block, now cottages.[^s2]

The manor house, known as Clifton Hall is situated on the right bank of the River Trent in the village of Clifton, Nottinghamshire,. about 3+1⁄2 miles south-west of the historic centre of the City of Nottingham, now partly the campus of Nottingham Trent University and partly a large council estate of modern housing.

stories.text: 56 Village Road began in 1319 as a timber-framed farmhouse, later enlarged and cased in brick; it keeps its thatched roof and much of its old timber inside, and is listed Grade II*. Its neighbour, 29 Village Road, is a timber-framed house of about 1500, also thatched and later made into two cottages.

stories.text: In 1958 a bridge opened here to take traffic off Trent Bridge. It was then the longest pre-stressed concrete bridge in the country, and a second bridge beside it, opened in 1972, made the crossing a dual carriageway.

65666.sum: Clifton Bridge is a road bridge spanning the River Trent and carrying the A52 road to the west of the city of Nottingham, in the county of Nottinghamshire, England. It was completed and opened to traffic in March 1958 and is constructed of pre-stressed concrete. It is the next upstream road crossing from the older famous Trent Bridge.

stories.text: The ice dancers Jayne Torvill and Christopher Dean come from Nottingham.[^s1][^s2][^s3] The square outside the ice centre is named Bolero Square after their Olympic routine.[^s1][^s2][^s3] Jayne Torvill was born in Clifton on 7 October 1957 and worked as an insurance clerk at Norwich Union before skating full-time; at Sarajevo in 1984 she and Christopher Dean won the gold with their free dance to Ravel's Boléro, which earned twelve perfect 6.0 marks.[^s3]

74549.sum: The National Ice Centre is located in Nottingham, England. It is situated just east of the city centre, close to the historic Lace Market area. The NIC was the first twin Olympic-sized ice pad facility in the UK, "heralding a new era in the development of ice skating".
